bibliographic.title: RIXS study of strain-tuned coupled valence and spin-state transition in epitaxial (Pr0.85Y0.15)0.7Ca0.3CoO3 films

bibliographic.abstract: Strain-tuned (Pr0 . 85Y0 . 15)0 . 7Ca0 . 3CoO3 thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. Here, we use Co L 2 , 3 and Pr M 4 , 5 X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), along with Co L 3 edge Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS), to probe the local electronic structure across the strain-controlled VSST in epitaxial (Pr,Y,Ca)CoO3 thin films. In compressively strained films on YAlO3 (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr4+ -like spectral weight, suppresses Co4+ -like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co3+ . The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co–O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La0 . 18Sr0 . 82Al0 . 59Ta0 . 41O3 (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local dd excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co4+ -like local excitations and a broader particle–hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co–O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.
